review_scope: Six full permission and push-protection reusable fragments read as inert source evidence. Linked pages, images and product-variable resolution remain pending. No rendered-page certificate or policy adoption.

claims.statement: The permission fragment lists repository owners, organization owners, security managers, enterprise administrators and admin-role users; its list is not proof that a particular actor has effective permissions.
The enable-push-protection option is documented as visible only for published patterns.
A custom-pattern dry run is documented as requiring administration access to the selected repository.
An enterprise owner wanting dry-run access across an organization's repositories must also be assigned its organization-owner role in the source guidance.
Enterprise custom-pattern push protection requires enterprise-level secret-scanning push protection enabled.
Enabling push protection for commonly occurring custom patterns may disrupt contributors.
The organization note repeats that enablement is visible only for published patterns.
Organization custom-pattern push protection applies only to repositories with secret-scanning push protection enabled; organization configuration alone does not establish repository coverage.
The organization note repeats the contributor-disruption risk for common custom patterns.
The reusable UI procedure makes selecting Enable for custom-pattern push protection optional; this is not an adopted mandatory obligation.
The editing-procedure note limits custom-pattern push protection to repositories whose secret-scanning push protection is enabled.
The editing-procedure note repeats contributor-disruption risk for common custom patterns.
